sermon.title: Your Adversary the Devil 05/20/2018
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: Pastor David G. Kincer shows that Satan opposes God even where God and scripture are understood. He disguises himself as an angel of light, works through corrupt ministers and lying wonders like Jim Jones, lied to Eve and stirred Cain to murder. From the beginning God has wanted people to do good, so believers should rule over sin, speak what is good like Abel, and be good like Barnabas.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added from the speaker’s pauses and then corrected by hand, and obvious caption errors (names, Bible references) were fixed; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor notes: Garbled words are marked [unclear]. Kept as spoken: Jim Jones “put a gun to his head and shot himself” and almost a thousand died (14:21–15:01). Unverified: Pope Damasus I killed rivals, committed adultery, sold women and children as slaves and prostituted nuns (2:07–4:21); Bill Clinton started his own Baptist church accepting abortion and homosexuality (41:57); the Disciples of Christ called Unitarian. Sensitive content kept as spoken: Catholic clergy abuse “caught all the time”. Addiction and pedophilia not diseases; California law could jail him (21:09–23:06). Poverty is “a smartphone color TV”; more welfare per baby (23:06). Women who object to slaughtering animals: “take your complaints to him” (25:00). Gun blame and “unsensible” America (29:00). Women “crank out a baby” (37:06). Kept as spoken: “Cain wasn’t being silent” where Abel is meant (38:04). The death penalty (42:54).

scriptures.text_nkjv: For he was a good man, full of the Holy Spirit and of faith. And a great many people were added to the Lord.

Though I speak with the tongues of men and of angels, but have not love, I have become sounding brass or a clanging cymbal. And though I have the gift of prophecy, and understand all mysteries and all knowledge, and though I have all faith, so that I could remove mountains, but have not love, I am nothing. And though I bestow all my goods to feed the poor, and though I give my body to be burned, but have not love, it profits me nothing.
